text: The direct answer to the client: with Rs 1,000 you cannot apply for Srit India at all. A mainboard (EQ) retail application is at least one lot, typically Rs 14,000-15,000 per the brief's IPO facts, so the budget is short by roughly 14x — the question 'what if I get allotted' is moot because the application itself is unaffordable. Even if it were affordable, SRIT's book is subscribed 9.94x and closes today (30-Sep), so a one-lot retail applicant's allotment chance is roughly 1 in 10, and the brief gives no fundamentals, GMP level, or peer pricing to judge value — only a headline that a GMP page exists. Context is sobering: recent listings are mixed (ArMee -15.9%, Varmora -5.0% vs Hero Motors +79.5%), and the Nifty is down 5.8% in a month with RSI 26, a weak tape for new listings. On costs, even a winning Rs 1,000-scale trade loses ~1.8-2.1% to charges (DP fee alone ~1.6%) and listing gains are taxed at 20% STCG. My honest advice: do nothing with the Rs 1,000; IPO lottery punts are not a route to the 10x goal, which needs ~21%/month for a year — lottery-like odds by definition.
